beats.say: Milk cost you seventy rupees in early May. Now it's seventy-six. But why, and who gets the extra?
Last Thursday, Mother Dairy and Amul both added up to four rupees a litre.
Second hike since May. Six rupees more, in six months.
So who's pocketing it? The dairy? The shop?
Neither, mostly. Amul says about eighty percent of what you pay goes back to its farmers.
So roughly three of your four rupees reach the farmer, who's paying more for cattle feed.
lines: Feed, fodder and fuel cost more
